local_review.finding_body: The required `javaTest` lane terminated with exit 134 in all three matrix jobs. The crash report identified `rs2_create_context` from `configuresPipelineForUnavailableDeviceWithoutStartingCapture`, and isolated reproduction showed that both full context-creation scenarios SIGSEGV in `pthread_mutex_lock` when no USB subsystem is available. Required tests must pass every configured Java and Native Image lane under §FS-repository-functional-spec.5.2; because the defect was confined to this contribution's tests, it was repaired under §FS-contribution-contract.5.1.
local_review.finding_title: Headless RealSense context creation crashes the test process
local_review.fix_note: Replaced the two hardware-discovery context scenarios with device-independent public-API coverage: native enum-to-string conversion and stream/device configuration on an `rs2_config` object. No test was disabled, skipped, or made native-only, and the suite still contains eight meaningful tests. Verified with headless Ubuntu 22.04 JVM and full current-defaults Native Image tests, a full future-defaults-all test on the available latest-EA GraalVM, and coordinate-scoped index, metadata, style, formatting, and stats checks. `generateLibraryStats` produced no committed stats change.
local_review.review_comment: All three required metadata-test jobs failed in the Java lane because the two tests that created a RealSense context triggered a native SIGSEGV in `pthread_mutex_lock` on headless Ubuntu. I reproduced the crash in a clean Ubuntu 22.04 container, isolated both context-creation scenarios, repaired the contribution locally, and reviewed the full single-coordinate diff against the new-library rules. The repaired eight-test suite passes JVM and Native Image execution in headless `current-defaults` and passes the `future-defaults-all` lane on the available latest-EA GraalVM; index, metadata, Checkstyle, Spotless, and stats validation also pass. The contribution is ready.
